item.text:
Best read: **mixed, but meaningfully more than slogans**. In 2024 Marcos did translate several declared priorities into decrees, laws, and administrative machinery. The strongest implementation evidence is in anti-poverty delivery, cybersecurity, procurement reform, and the POGO shutdown. The main weakness is that some headline claims remained branding-heavy, and some flagship economic promises had only partial or delayed pass-through.

**Accepted claim items**

- **[EO 52, Institutionalizing the Pag-Abot Program, Constituting An Inter-Agency Committee Therefor, and for Other Purposes](https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2024/eo_52_2024.html)** | Lawphil / Office of the President | 2024-01-18 | Marcos converted anti-poverty rhetoric into a standing program with an inter-agency committee, monitoring, and biannual reporting. | QIDs: 8B.6

- **[PBBM approves National Cybersecurity Plan to fortify PH against various threats](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-approves-national-cybersecurity-plan-to-fortify-ph-against-various-threats/)** | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-02-08 | The administration moved from cybersecurity talk to a formal plan with policy direction and operational guidelines, signaling institutional follow-through rather than pure sloganizing. | QIDs: 8B.6

- **[PBBM Signs Laws on Streamlining Procurement, Combatting Online Scams](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-laws-on-streamlining-procurement-combatting-online-scams/)** | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-20 | Marcos backed procurement rules that standardized forms and institutionalized e-procurement, which is concrete state-capacity building and a real anti-favoritism mechanism. | QIDs: 8B.6

- **[PBBM bans all POGOs](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-bans-all-pogos/)** | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-22 | A high-profile SONA promise became a formal ban with a wind-down order and labor reabsorption steps, showing a declaration turning into enforceable state action. | QIDs: 8B.6

- **[BI: 24K foreign POGO workers leave PH](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1240226)** | Philippine News Agency | 2024-12-18 | This shows the POGO ban moved into observable enforcement by year-end, not just announcement. | QIDs: 8B.6

- **[PBBM orders activation of online platform to monitor El Nino-La Nina phenomena](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-activation-of-online-platform-to-monitor-el-nino-la-nina-phenomena/)** | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-03-26 | Marcos paired crisis rhetoric with monitoring infrastructure and public reporting, which is a concrete form of state reach. | QIDs: 8B.6

- **[PBBM orders 4Ps expansion to cover pregnant, lactating women](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-4ps-expansion-to-cover-pregnant-lactating-women-to-ensure-childrens-health-well-being-in-first-1000-days/)** | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-06-11 | A declared welfare priority was turned into a specific program change aimed at maternal-child health. | QIDs: 8B.6

**Counterevidence / limits**

- **[Marcos: Bagong Pilipinas a set of ideals, not a new partisan group](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/895658/marcos-bagong-pilipinas-set-of-ideals-not-a-new-partisan-group/story/)** | GMA News Online | 2024-01-28 | The opening frame was branding-heavy and self-descriptive; by itself it did not demonstrate delivery or administrative change. | QIDs: 8B.6

- **[Sona 2024 fact check](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1964296/sona-2024-fact-check)** | Philippine Daily Inquirer | 2024-07-23 | Independent fact-checking found Marcos’s explanation of rice inflation was incomplete or inaccurate, which undercuts the sense that public framing cleanly matched reality. | QIDs: 8B.6

- **[NEDA: Reduced rice tariffs failed to lower prices](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/economy/929579/neda-reduced-rice-tariffs-failed-to-lower-prices/story/)** | GMA News Online | 2024-12-10 | The flagship rice-affordability intervention had only partial or no pass-through, so not all declared goals became observable outcomes. | QIDs: 8B.6

- **[Philippines | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines)** | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | Press-freedom problems, red-tagging, blocked sites, and threats persisted, showing some public claims about openness were not converted into a safer state environment. | QIDs: 8B.6

- **[USDOS 2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Philippines](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128580.html)** | U.S. Department of State | 2024 | The report says threats by government, allied groups, and powerful individuals against critics continued, which limits any claim that rhetoric about safety translated into a cleanly protective state. | QIDs: 8B.6

**Bottom line**

Marcos in 2024 **did not just speak in slogans**: he repeatedly turned priorities into executive orders, laws, reporting systems, and enforcement steps. But the record is also **not a clean execution story**: some flagship claims were branding-heavy, and some policy goals, especially rice affordability and civic openness, showed only partial or contested translation into outcomes.

**Search gap**

I found **strong official evidence for implementation mechanics** on Pag-Abot, cybersecurity, procurement, and POGO closure, but **limited independent downstream evaluation** for those exact programs within the 6-call search budget. The most independent outcome-style evidence I found was for rice policy, where the pass-through was mixed and often disappointing.
